hints: Notice extension is not read directly but found from $250 \text{ mm}$ minus $225 \text{ mm}$, giving $25 \text{ mm}$.
Recall that for addition or subtraction the absolute uncertainties add, so combine the two $\pm 2 \text{ mm}$ values.
Connect the combined $4 \text{ mm}$ uncertainty to the small $25 \text{ mm}$ extension using $(\text{absolute uncertainty} / \text{value}) \times 100\%$.
walkthrough: Find the extension from the two pointer positions: $250 \text{ mm} - 225 \text{ mm} = 25 \text{ mm}$.
State the rule for a difference: absolute uncertainties add. Each position has $\pm 2 \text{ mm}$.
Add them: absolute uncertainty in extension $= 2 \text{ mm} + 2 \text{ mm} = 4 \text{ mm}$.
The small $25 \text{ mm}$ difference makes the percentage large, which rules out using $225 \text{ mm}$ or $250 \text{ mm}$ in the denominator. This is option D.

options.A: This is $4 \text{ mm}$ divided by the final $250 \text{ mm}$ reading. Percentage uncertainty must use the $25 \text{ mm}$ extension, not a single scale reading.
options.B: This is $4 \text{ mm}$ divided by the initial $225 \text{ mm}$ reading. Percentage uncertainty must use the calculated $25 \text{ mm}$ difference.
options.C: This uses only one $\pm 2 \text{ mm}$ uncertainty. Extension needs two readings so absolute uncertainties add to $4 \text{ mm}$.
options.D: Extension is $25 \text{ mm}$ with absolute uncertainty $2+2=4 \text{ mm}$, so $(4/25)\times 100\% = 16\%$.
